newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Accor sees slight tax impact.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Accor sees slight tax impact.

text.p: Accor chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux said on Wednesday that the group expected to be only slightly affected by a rise in tax on corporate profit in France.
"We will be only slightly affected in the years 1997 to 1999 because of the fiscal situation of the Accor parent company," he told Reuters in an interview.

He said subsidiaries that were not consolidated, such as casino company SPIC, would be affected by the tax rise announced last month as part of the new government's plan to cut the deficit as a proportion of gross domestic product.

Market operators had said they expected Accor to be one of the groups hardest hit by the increase in tax on profits and capital gains, imposed to help France meet the criteria for European monetary union.
Accor announced in June that it had raised its stake in SPIC, France's fourth-largest casino company, to 65 percent.
